- Two invocations sharing runTag preserve distinct single/split review artifacts and current reviewPath/null semantics.
- A blocked review followed by a silent or ready retry retains earlier actionable findings and their source.
- Interrupted collection resumes without overwriting artifacts, duplicating occurrences or losing supported dispositions.
- Complete extraction includes deferred items without changing existing --keys output.
- Deferred findings leave the punch list only after explicit supported resolution or rejection, including fixes supplied elsewhere.
- Task success, closed fix beads and silence alone leave findings outstanding.
- Explicit references link appearances; uncertain matches remain separate; rejection retains its basis.
- Missing artifacts and unsupported projections retain unresolved evidence and expose the gap.
- Resume, Remaining and status qualifiers consume the same outstanding projection; latest ready cannot conceal earlier findings.
- Deterministic producer/extraction/projection fixtures cover both execution paths. The enclosing coordinator owns fresh-agent interrupted-invocation and changed-instruction evaluations.

decision: patch
summary: Apply bounded repairs to existing components and complete the named review/evidence gaps; independent defects and repeated confirmations do not justify redesign, and caller-owned sweep/acceptance obligations remain separate.
pattern: First code round, with no failed patch history. Repeated confirmations concern archive integrity (r1 [Should-fix] skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:168), recursive archive assembly (r1 [Should-fix] skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:224), and TMPDIR normalization (r1 [Should-fix] tests/super-code/test-dispatch-text.sh:10); each pair has one cause and one local fix. Recovery-scope preservation, deterministic invocation startup, immutable source binding on resume, complete projection output, symlink-safe collection, outer cleanup ordering, missing retained artifacts and unsupported profile claims need distinct repairs under existing invariants. In particular, invocation identity/source binding and excluding prior generated inputs are bounded corrections to current review components, not grounds for another archive or workflow engine. The three unreviewed clusters require their own unambiguous bounded coverage; archived-copy scope limits and the intentionally pending final sweep, behavioral assessment, platform-specific verification and root/human acceptance remain qualified obligations, not additional demonstrated product defects. Retain the roast's supported measurement-classification rejection and direct frozen-Git fallback rejection: fixing repeated recursive amplification does not overturn the latter's narrower materiality judgment.
clusters:
- archive-integrity: r1 [Should-fix] skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:168, r1 [Must-fix] [P2; cluster 56] `skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:168`: validate current archived existence/hashes at the read-only acceptance gate. Lines 293–296 inspect only persisted collection complete/gaps metadata. After valid collection, the cluster corrupted the direct `.md.diff`; acceptance still returned exit 0, `eligible:true`, empty pending/gaps, while collection replay returned exit 3 with `archive conflict`. Source evidence: cluster-56.md and its owned fixture; test missing/corrupted archive inputs without requiring mutating recollection first. | rule: At the existing read-only status/acceptance boundary, validate every retained collection file against its saved existence and hash before trusting complete metadata; missing or changed bytes remain evidence gaps without requiring recollection.
- generated-input-recursion: r1 [Should-fix] skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:224, r1 [Must-fix] [P2; seam] `skills/super-auto/scripts/report-status:223` / `skills/super-auto/SKILL.md:400` → `skills/super-code/assembler-prompt.md:26`: prevent committed generated review inputs from recursively re-entering subsequent full-branch assemblies while retaining historical provenance. Source evidence: captured collector/assembler/caller source, `/private/tmp/ufz-seam-amplification-probe.py`, owned `.review-probes/recursive-archive-result.json`, and this report's companion package; cover repeated successful collection/re-entry without further code changes. | rule: Exclude prior collected generated review-input trees from subsequent full-range slice assembly while retaining their immutable archives and explicit provenance references; apply the same boundary on every review re-entry.

section: ## Lingering B4 result and its limits
text: The two failures explicitly withhold acceptance. The other three neither establish the missing records nor explicitly declare V9 pending, so conditional language is preserved as ambiguity, not credited as a pass or silently relabeled a failure. Thus 5/5 unconditional acceptance is not demonstrated. Under a binary rule counting every unproven acceptance as failure, the same raw answers would be 0 pass / 5 not-demonstrated; the recorded three-way scoring retains the distinction.

section: ## Other decisions and unresolved scenario ambiguity
text: Every A response pins `1a11` against `0b00`, leaves the caller on `2c22`, confines writing reproduction to the review worktree, declines causal damage attribution from a checkout difference, reports shutdown unconfirmed after denied discovery, preserves owned resources, and leaves the unrelated server alone.

The evaluator read installed `writing-skills/SKILL.md`, its `testing-skills-with-subagents.md` pressure-evaluation reference and required TDD background. Respondents used **gpt-6.1-sol / medium / fork_turns=none**, one fresh agent per case/repetition. The baseline wrapper, role and exact scenario bytes were reused; only guidance/scenario paths were substituted. Rubric, earlier results, score counts and this report were never supplied to respondents. All complete final responses were manually read and scored claim by claim; evidence quotations are retained per claim in `scores.json`.

Selection preserves the baseline’s logical operative sections and whole clauses. Expanded new contracts include verification-only selection in the full task reviewer; adjacent bundle identity before worktree topology; the final-review/continuity/collection contracts surrounding Phase 6; task-base/run-baseline attribution; the expanded whole upstream Process; and updated output process tags. The broader reference is actual committed product text, not proposed wording. Exact selection is a visible experimental input, and comparison does not isolate any single sentence’s causal effect.

| A1 stable revision/no caller switch, A2 caller-file isolation, A3 no damage attribution/reset from comparison alone, A4 unknown cleanup, A5 resources/ownership | Each 0/5 | Each 0/5 |

- B-baseline-3: “the supplied ordinary reviewer rules explicitly require **INVALID**”; it routed V9 to an “explicitly authorized verification-only acceptance path.”
- B-baseline-4: “V9 cannot be marked fully complete through that review path,” pending “a legitimate verification-only acceptance mechanism.”

`after-pack.json` prepares the unchanged cases, model, fresh-agent policy, five repetitions per case, source-freezing requirements, and private claim rubric. R1 Reviews use stable source revisions and isolated mutable outputs without modifying the caller checkout.
R2 Cleanup reports verified stopped, surviving, unknown and deliberate preservation accurately, retaining resources still needed by owned processes.
R3 Dispatch rechecks admission after capacity waits and observes external dependency closure without blocking unrelated eligible work on failed lookups.
R4 Durable recovery facts preserve holds, pending closure, deferred obligations and fix history; resume reconciles Git/tracker evidence and reuses valid work.
R5 Source-bound evidence preserves command/configuration, outcome and location, distinguishing live/simulated/fallback and failed/unavailable checks.
R6 Reviewed verification-only tasks may finish without artificial commits while implementation tasks retain delivery requirements.
R7 Caller-owned measurement and acceptance remain explicit; completed leaves cannot close a super-auto root with outstanding required obligations.
R8 Task-base exoneration cannot erase ownership of a regression introduced earlier in the run; missing run-baseline evidence remains a gap.
R9 Immutable invocation reviews and explicit finding identities retain unresolved findings across retries until supported disposition.
R10 Deferred findings fixed elsewhere resolve only after verification; uncertain matches remain separate and rejection retains reasoning/evidence.
R11 Narrow process-class aliases preserve original text and distinguish defect identity, severity and scope.
R12 Deterministic metrics distinguish transport gaps and valid-empty data, incorporate reconciliation, and report supported partial results with observed ID discrepancies.
R13 Metrics separate latest attempt/run history, repaired/deferred/rejected findings, task landings/base absorption and execution metadata/friction.
R14 Profiler timing respects task existence and evidenced readiness, preserves unknowns, labels observed graph/concurrency scope and includes planning in diagnosis with estimates identified.
R15 Existing execution paths and caller/standalone boundaries remain covered by focused mechanics fixtures, representative agent behavior evaluations and a root integration sweep.

Two valid fresh same-family reviews completed. Reviewer1 used normalized ID aliases in compact input; reviewer2 received verbatim scripted Goals/tree. Both map all R1–R15. Two detail-omission candidates rejected to ledger; no task changes applied. No second round required. Root sweep super-plan-ufz.14 added after coverage, depending on 16 leaves.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.1 — LEAF — Pin review inputs and isolate mutable reproductions
text: Bind review source and diff inputs to captured commit identities. Prefer read-only Git retrieval; when filesystem access is needed use a review-owned detached worktree, with isolated mutable build/reproduction outputs. Do not switch or restore the caller checkout. Cover task/final and adversarial reviews using their existing dispatch components. The coordinator owns fresh-agent pressure evaluation; the implementer prepares deterministic fixtures and the behavioral acceptance scenario.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.1 — LEAF — Pin review inputs and isolate mutable reproductions
text:
Acceptance:
- [ ] A review remains pinned to its captured SHAs while the caller integration branch advances.
- [ ] A reproduction that writes files leaves the caller checkout and another review's mutable outputs untouched.
- [ ] A changed caller checkout is reported with evidence without attributing damage solely from before/after differences or restoring the old snapshot.
- [ ] The coordinator records representative fresh-agent evaluation of changed review instructions; deterministic input/dispatch fixtures pass.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.2 — LEAF — Propagate cleanup uncertainty and retain needed resources
text: Carry verified stopped, surviving, unknown and deliberately kept outcomes through existing process/worktree helpers, coordinator Finish, ordinary-subagent instructions and super-auto reporting. Preserve needed worktree/temp resources when owned processes survive or cannot be verified. Do not widen process matching. Keep the helper and its callers together because current worktree cleanup discards stop failure before deleting resources. The coordinator owns any fresh-agent evaluation of changed caller instructions.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.2 — LEAF — Propagate cleanup uncertainty and retain needed resources
text:
Acceptance:
- [ ] Denied discovery or status inspection cannot produce stopped or a verified nothing-running result.
- [ ] A surviving or unverified owned process retains the worktree/temp resources it may still need and those resources are identified in the result.
- [ ] Verified termination permits normal cleanup; deliberately preserved resources remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Unrelated processes remain outside cleanup targets, and code delivery can be reported alongside incomplete cleanup.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.3 — LEAF — Recheck admission and refresh external dependency readiness
text: Within the existing scheduler, recheck hold/cancellation/dependency admission after acquiring capacity and before dispatch. Distinguish local implementation readiness from tracker review/blocker/human-gate closure. Refresh external readiness at bounded opportunities while work is in flight. A failed lookup holds only affected work. Exercise both Workflow mechanics and ordinary-subagent contract; the coordinator owns live ordinary-subagent evaluation.

section: ## super-plan-ufz.3 — LEAF — Recheck admission and refresh external dependency readiness
text:
Acceptance:
- [ ] A hold established during a slot wait prevents dispatch; the slot is released and no implementation attempt is falsely reported.
- [ ] A closed external review dependency releases its consumer even when its ID is absent from implementation completion sets.
- [ ] An external release becomes visible while a long-running task remains in flight.
- [ ] A failed dependency lookup keeps affected work held with a reason while unrelated eligible work continues.
- [ ] Deterministic Workflow replay covers both execution-path contracts; coordinator-owned live evaluation checks changed ordinary-subagent instructions.

Retain actual transcript, prior/new source identities, collection files and final projections. This should not close any real root or invent human acceptance.

Several cases may share one packet and sample; report independent sample counts rather than counting cases as respondents.

Include this small case in the relevant current resume-context packet. No need to replay the entire historical design run.
